audience.text: Python developers building document processing applications who need a pure-Python, dependency-light alternative to Microsoft Word automation for DOCX, DOC, RTF, Markdown, and plain-text files.

capabilities.text: Automatically selects the appropriate reader (DOCX, DOC, RTF, Markdown, or plain text) based on file extension when constructing a Document.
capabilities.title: Read multiple input formats

capabilities.text: Parses DOCX files using only the standard library zipfile and xml.etree modules, with no compiled dependencies.
capabilities.title: Pure-Python DOCX parsing

capabilities.text: Reads Word 97-2003 .doc binary files and RTF documents via olefile delegation.
capabilities.title: Legacy DOC support

capabilities.text: Embeds inline, captioned, table, and header/footer images as base64 data URIs in Markdown, renders them in PDF, and preserves them losslessly in DOCX round-trips.
capabilities.title: Image handling

capabilities.text: Exports to Markdown using LdmMarkdownWriter with tunable options for heading style, list markers, code blocks, tables, links, and image embedding.
capabilities.title: Markdown export with options

capabilities.text: Exports to PDF using LdmPdfWriter backed by fpdf2, with built-in paragraph, table, and shape rendering and configurable options.
capabilities.title: PDF export with fpdf2

capabilities.text: Exposes a Light Document Model built with Pydantic models for sections, paragraphs, runs, tables, styles, and lists.
capabilities.title: Typed document model

limitations.text: SaveFormat.DOC is defined for API compatibility but Document.save() does not implement a DOC writer; saving to DOC raises ValueError.
OoxmlSaveOptions.compliance set to ISO29500_2008_STRICT raises NotImplementedError; only ECMA376_2006 and ISO29500_2008_TRANSITIONAL are implemented.

Eight PdfSaveOptions fields (text_compression, embed_full_fonts, use_core_fonts, font_embedding_mode, page_mode, color_mode, preserve_form_fields, memory_optimization) are not yet consumed by the PDF writer.

problems_solved.text: Enables pure-Python document processing without requiring Microsoft Word, COM automation, or system-level Office dependencies.
Provides a unified Light Document Model to parse and convert between DOCX, DOC, RTF, Markdown, and plain-text formats.
Supports round-trip editing of DOCX files while preserving headers, footers, images, bookmarks, and custom styles.

product_summary.text: Aspose.Words FOSS for Python is a free, open-source, MIT-licensed Python library for reading and writing Word documents without Microsoft Word or COM automation.

workflows.name: Load and convert document
workflows.text: Construct a Document from a file path, then call save() with a SaveFormat constant or options instance to export to DOCX, Markdown, PDF, or plain text.

workflows.name: Parse Markdown with structure
workflows.text: Load Markdown files using MarkdownFileReader so headings, lists, emphasis, tables, and embedded images become typed nodes in the Light Document Model.

workflows.name: Export to PDF with built-in renderer
workflows.text: Use LdmPdfWriter backed by fpdf2 to render paragraphs, tables, and shapes to PDF without external engines or system fonts.

workflows.name: Extract plain text
workflows.text: Call Document.get_text() or save with SaveFormat.TEXT to extract plain text from any loaded document.
